content: Recursive watch limits: Linux inotify = one watch per subdirectory; fs.inotify.max_user_watches default 8192 (older kernels) or RAM-scaled 8,192-1,048,576 (kernel 5.11+); instances default 128; queued events 16384. node_modules/.venv-scale trees blow past 8192. CRITICAL: recursive-watch exhaustion can fail SILENTLY - notify issue #109: recursive watch ran out of watches with NO error set (non-recursive raises cryptic ENOSPC 'No space left on device'); symptom = events from some subtrees never arrive. Kernel IN_Q_OVERFLOW discards events when queue overflows -> Watchman recrawls entire tree; Watchman treats un-watchable dir as poisoned, fails ALL watches until process restart. macOS FSEvents: one stream per root, scales well (500GB tree fine); kFSEventStreamEventFlagUserDropped when kernel limit exceeded - raise fsevents latency; no per-dir watch limit. Prevention: exclude heavy subtrees (.git, node_modules) from the watch (watchdog schedules recursive watches over EVERYTHING under root - ignore filtering must happen at watch setup not just event handling), catch emitter errors, log watch count, rescan fallback on overflow. Sources: syncovery inotify limits, Watchman troubleshooting docs, notify issue 109, shire PR 290 (ENOSPC production crash).
